course.title: The Rise of the Roman Empire
course.description: Follow Rome from a republic of elected magistrates to an empire governed from one city, and see what survived it.

lessons.title: The rise of the Roman Empire
lessons.orientation: Look at how far Roman rule eventually reached, then work backwards to the moment one man came to hold it.

lessons.title: Expansion and the provinces
lessons.orientation: Look at the paving in the photograph and ask what a surface like that made possible for a state governed from one city.

lessons.title: Life in the city, and what outlasted it
lessons.orientation: Look closely at the scale of the amphitheatre in the photograph, then use the timeline to compare the dated events that follow it.

modules.title: From republic to empire
modules.description: Trace how Rome's shared republican authority gave way to rule by one man, and how that state was held together afterwards.

concepts.title: The Roman Republic
concepts.summary: The Republic governed Rome from 509 BCE through elected magistrates and a senate of former office-holders.

concepts.title: The crisis of the Republic
concepts.summary: Commanders who held long military commands and personal armies broke the Republic's habit of shared, temporary power.

concepts.title: Augustus and the principate
concepts.summary: Augustus kept the outward forms of the Republic while holding the legal powers that made him sole ruler.

concepts.title: Roman expansion
concepts.summary: War and annexation carried Roman rule around the Mediterranean and into western Europe over roughly four centuries.

concepts.title: Provinces and administration
concepts.summary: A province was governed by an appointed official who kept order and answered to Rome for the taxes it produced.

concepts.title: Roman roads
concepts.summary: Paved military roads let armies and official messages travel at a speed the state could plan around.

concepts.title: Roman citizenship
concepts.summary: Citizenship carried legal standing under Roman law and was extended to provincial populations over time.

concepts.title: Life in the Roman city
concepts.summary: Urban life centred on public buildings paid for by emperors and wealthy citizens, from bath houses to the amphitheatre.

concepts.title: The end of western rule and what followed
concepts.summary: Imperial rule ended in the west in 476 CE while the eastern half continued, and Roman law and Latin outlived both.
